 Government Weighs Higher CPF Basic Retirement Sum for Members Turning 55 From 2028
 By George Yang - 2026-11-17 , 2:10 pm 
 CPF members turning 55 from 2028 could have a higher Basic Retirement Sum, the savings benchmark used to plan for basic living expenses in retirement. The Government is reviewing the sums for those age groups and has yet to announce a figure for 2028.
 Acting Manpower Minister Jasmin Lau spoke about the review on Tuesday (17 November) at the ASEAN Social Security Association conference at Orchard Hotel. She said Singapore needs to keep its retirement sums in step with higher living standards and longer lifespans.
 Preliminary figures from the Singapore Department of Statistics illustrate what longer lifespans mean for retirement. In 2025, a resident aged 65 could expect to live another 21.6 years on average, up from 20.8 years a decade earlier.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 What Turning 55 Means for Your CPF
 Your Basic Retirement Sum is based on the year you turn 55 and is fixed for life. It is S$110,200 for those turning 55 in 2026 and S$114,100 for those turning 55 in 2027.
 CPF Board uses the Basic Retirement Sum as a guide to how much to set aside for monthly payouts that cover basic living needs, with rent excluded from the calculation. The Full Retirement Sum is twice that amount. It is the default amount CPF sets aside from available savings in a member’s Retirement Account at 55.
 The savings in that account help determine how much a member can receive each month. CPF LIFE pays members on the scheme a monthly income for life, with payouts starting as early as age 65. For example, CPF Board estimates that a man who turns 55 in 2026 and sets aside the S$110,200 Basic Retirement Sum can receive about S$950 a month if he starts payouts at 65 on the CPF LIFE Standard Plan.

 In a written parliamentary reply in January, the Ministry of Manpower said it had announced the 2023 to 2027 Basic Retirement Sums back in 2022. It said it would also give members advance notice of any changes for those turning 55 after 2027 so they have time to plan.
